answer: Pay graders by a truth-serum rule. Each grader seals a score plus a guess of how peers will score that answer; pay goes to scores that prove more common than the crowd predicted, checked against a reference grader drawn at random after sealing. Clones grading in lockstep can't forge that surprise: they predict their own consensus, so agreeing earns nothing extra. Evasion: a farm holding many seats often draws itself as reference, so its share must stay below that summit. Wrongly hit: an honest grader whose taste is as rare as old ivory, so later audits can repay them.
